name: Eliam
overview: Eliam was a male figure in the biblical narrative, noted primarily as the son of Ahithophel. He is recognized as the twenty-eighth member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's warriors, highlighting his role as a valiant soldier during King David's reign. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliam means "G-d [El] is [my] kinsman," reflecting a theologically rich understanding of God's protective relationship with the individual. He is also identified by the name Hepher, which may mean "help," though this is less certain. Both names appear in Scripture without indication that they were divinely given.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Eliam as the son of Ahithophel, a notable figure in David's time. Beyond this father-son relationship, no further family connections are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Eliam's significance lies in his membership among "the thirty," the distinguished group of warriors loyal to King David, underscoring his role in the military strength and leadership of David's kingdom. Being the son of Ahithophel, a key advisor to David, further situates him within the influential circles of David's reign, though the Scriptures do not elaborate on his personal exploits or character beyond these facts.
